statement: If [p]_F lies in pR[[t]] + t^q R[[t]] (q = p^h) over a p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebra R, then D^n f lies in p^(a_h(n)) R[[t]] for every integral f, with a_h(n) = max{E_h(n), ceil(c_h n - (h-1)), 0}, c_h = 1/(p-1) - 1/(q-1), E_h(n) the sum of floor(n/p^j) over j not divisible by h; the constant h-1, the slope c_h and the floor sum at the powers of p are optimal.

At height two, D^n f lies in p^(a_2(n)) R[[t]] with a_2(n) = max{sum_r floor(n/p^(2r+1)), ceil(np/(p^2-1)) - 1, 0}; so Katz's bound floor(np/(p^2-1)) holds for every integral f unless p^2 - 1 divides n, where it can fail by one and does fail at n = p^2 - 1.

A formal group law over a p-torsion-free W(F_q)-algebra with an action of the Teichmuller roots of unity lifting multiplication on the tangent space satisfies the hypothesis of Theorem A; in particular every formal W(F_q)-module does.

Over W(k)[varpi] with varpi^e = p, e >= 2, there is a formal group law whose special fibre has height h and with (D^p t)(0) = (p-1)! varpi, of valuation 1/e < 1; for e > p the valuations along the powers of p grow with slope 1/(e(p-1)) < c_2.

The d-dimensional law H (d = h-1) with logarithm sum_n p^(-n) M^n(X) has coefficients in Z_p, its p-divisible group is over W(F_q) the Cartier dual of that of the Honda group G_h, and its invariant derivations satisfy D_i^n f in p^(max{0, ceil(c_i n - 1)}) with c_i = p^i/(q-1), sum c_i = c_h; slopes and constant optimal.
